method.source: SEC EDGAR: Schedule 13E-3 transaction statements and the proxy statements attached to or filed with them (dealType take-private), and DEFM14A / DEFM14C definitive merger proxies found through the quarterly form index (dealType public merger); XBRL company facts for the target's financials
method.acquirer: for a take-private, the buyer a page names from the 13E-3 filer list; for a merger proxy, the first named party of the merger agreement sentence that is neither the target nor a merger vehicle (acquirerBasis is the sentence), null where the parties are named only by defined term or the reading names no one (a sentence fragment such as 'Inc.', the merger vehicle, the target's own general partner); the primary then takes the buyer the latest reading of the deal names (filledFrom.acquirer). acquirerReader is the version of this rule
method.target: the company whose holders are paid: for a merger proxy, the registrant, under the name it filed under (the form index; currentName is EDGAR's name today, where the company has since been renamed, often for the vehicle merged into it), unless the proxy pays another company's holders in the registrant's own stock or puts a split-off to its own holders, when the row is set aside (status) with targetBasis the sentences; for a take-private, the subject company the deck index or the 13E-3 filer list names, and a statement the deck index files under another deal takes that deal's subject. targetReader is this rule's version
method.dealId: one transaction: the target's CIK and the date of its earliest reading. A deal read from several filings (a 13E-3 and its proxy, a proxy and its supplement) has one primary row, the latest filing to state an offer; the others are status 'duplicate' with duplicateOf the primary and their own reading kept under readStatus. readings lists every filing of the deal, offerHistory the offers they state where they differ, filledFrom the reading each borrowed field came from. Two buyers each named by the filings are two deals, unless each is a party to the other's agreement; a second deal for one target that starts on the same day carries its buyer after the date
method.status: ok, duplicate (another reading of a deal on file under duplicateOf), no-offer (read, no per-share cash figure stated), no-consideration (an acquirer-side vote: the filer's own holders voted on issuing shares, or a joint proxy whose registrant issues the shares and so is the buyer, acquirerSideBasis the sentences that say so, or a proxy that pays another company's holders in the registrant's own stock, targetBasis the sentences), rejected (a blank-check shell, a fund reorganisation, a split-off the registrant puts to its own holders (targetBasis), or a tender offer for warrants, notes or dividend-bearing preferred stock rather than the company's equity: not a precedent transaction; error says which, and securitiesSought the class the 13E-3 cover names) or error
method.announced: the merger agreement date as stated in the transaction statement; the 13E-3 filing date when no agreement date is stated (announcedBasis). announcedReader is the date rule's version: 2 reads only the deal's own agreement (a merger, arrangement, transaction, implementation or business combination agreement, or the purchase, sale, contribution or share exchange agreement of an asset sale or share purchase), never a credit, settlement, lease, confidentiality, voting or financing agreement the proxy recites. A date moves only when that version, the target or the classification does, and the LTM financials move with it
method.reverseMergerBasis: dealType 'reverse-merger': the proxy states that a private company's holders will own the majority (60% or more) of the listed company and its current holders the rest; the sentence and both stakes are kept. Such a row is not a control acquisition of the listed company
method.spacEvidence: for a merger proxy, how often its documents mention a trust account, an initial business combination, a blank-check company and a special purpose acquisition company; a proxy with at least 100 of the first and 5 of any other is a de-SPAC and rejected (spacRule 2), whatever its counterparty is called
method.offerPrice: per-share cash consideration as stated in the filing: the figure stated most often (offerBasis is the phrase matched), never a proposal, framework or bid the background recites, the issuer's own repurchase or self-tender, or a share count printed with a dollar sign; a stored price the reader now refuses everywhere is withdrawn and offerWithdrawn says why (offerReader 6)
method.offerImplied: the whole offer per share (offerReader 4): the cash of an all-cash deal, or a package with stock, an all-stock deal included, at the value its filing states for it on the last trading day before the announcement, as the agreed price or on a date near the agreement ('stated', offerImpliedDate), or as the filing works it from its own parts, an exchange ratio times the acquirer's stated close, plus any cash ('computed from stated components'). A value stated only at the proxy's practicable date is never the offer, no ratio is assumed and no price looked up: such a row carries offerUnresolved instead. offerComponents keeps every part with its passage and document; consideration is 'stock' where no cash is part of the package. premiumTie says whether the premium was checked against the whole offer: a stock package's premium is checked only on the day the package is valued, or where its stated price reproduces it
method.premiums: as the filing states them for its own deal, to the unaffected close (the last trading day before the news, as the filing defines it), the 30-trading-day VWAP and the 52-week high; a financial adviser's analysis (an illustrative range, comparable deals), an earlier proposal and the terms of another instrument (a capped call's cap, a conversion, exercise or strike price) are never read as the deal's premium, nor, for an all-cash deal, a statement whose reference price plus its premium is not the final offer to within two points (another bid's), unless it names the agreed consideration. premiumStatements lists every statement kept with its document, premiumsSetAside the ones left out and why, premiumBasis the sentences chosen. A 30-day VWAP or 52-week-high premium measured to the same day as a kept unaffected statement is kept with sharesReference true, and fills only a basis the agreement window left empty; a premium is borrowed from another reading only where that reading states the same offer
method.unaffectedGapDays: days from unaffectedDate to announced; a row whose gap exceeds 90 days is flagged 'long-unaffected-window: ...' with its premiums in doubt, and keeps the filing's own unaffected price. premiumPreAnnouncement (and its date) is the premium the filing states to the last close before the announcement, where it states one
method.announcedBasis: merger agreement (the agreement's date as stated), amended merger agreement (a revised deal: the latest amendment or restatement, where the filings state that it revised the agreed price to the row's offer; announcedOriginal the first agreement's date, which also dates the deal's dealId) or filing date (no agreement date stated)
method.unaffectedPrice: the closing price the filing states for the unaffected date (unaffectedPriceMethod 'stated', unaffectedDate the date); for an all-cash deal whose filing states only the percentage, offer / (1 + premium1Day) ('computed from the offer and the stated premium'); none for a deal paid partly in stock. vwap30 and high52 are offer / (1 + premium), all-cash deals only
method.financials: USD millions; sharesOut from the transaction statement when the company facts carry no count at announcement: the count of shares (common, ordinary or Class A) or common units it states as outstanding, never of ADSs, the most often stated; a count of shares issuable under or underlying options, awards, RSUs, warrants, convertibles or plans, reserved, held in treasury, authorized, a holding stated as a percentage of the outstanding, a count of preferred stock, or a count of another company's shares (one whose words name an issuer other than the target) is passed over, and where the statement gives no other there is no count and no equity value; a count is the target's when its words name the target by its name, the name its own filing's cover gives (a former name), a ticker or a short name the documents define for it, and a count that names the target beats one that names no one; where the documents state the count of each of the target's share classes, the count is the sum of the classes the filing shows receive the merger consideration (sharesBasis.classes names them and sharesBasis.terms quotes the clause), a class it shows has no economic interest, is cancelled for no consideration or is paid a nominal sum for its votes is left out and named with the reason (sharesBasis.excluded), a class exchanged into the paid class before the merger counts with it, where the filing prices each class reliably each is counted at its own price (sharesBasis.classPrices, with the passage), and a class whose terms it does not show leaves no count and no equity value (statedSharesClasses.why); LTM to the last fiscal period end on or before announcement (fiscal year + YTD - prior YTD), EBITDA = operating income + D&A, net debt = debt - cash and short-term investments at the same balance sheet; sharesOut = cover-page shares (dei) at the last cover date on or before announcement, millions. Revenue is the filed total: a larger Revenues figure for the same period replaces a part of it (a REIT's contract revenue beside its rent). A figure under $1m keeps thousands, so 0.0 means the filing says zero. companyFactsMissing is the day EDGAR last answered that it has no company facts for the target; such a row keeps what it has and is asked again after 183 days
method.values: equityValue = offerPrice x sharesOut, both per share (equityValueBasis says so): sharesOut is a count of shares, never of ADSs, and an offer quoted only per ADS with no ratio stated gives no equity value; where sharesBasis.classPrices prices the classes apart, equityValue is the sum of each class's count times its own price (a class priced at the offer at the offer per share); ev = equityValue + netDebt; dealValue = the aggregate value from the filing-fee table, kept as a cross-check; evLtmEbit = ev / ltmEbit, LTM operating income to ltmEbitEnd, kept whether or not EBITDA could be built
method.periods: each multiple has one period: EV at the deal against LTM revenue to ltmRevenueEnd (revenueTag the concept read), or against LTM EBITDA to ltmEbitdaEnd, whose operating income and D&A end within a week of each other. Revenue and D&A fall back to a utility's or a goods company's own concepts only where none of the usual ones is current. ltmImpairment is the impairment the filing tags inside the EBITDA's twelve months; at 10% of EBITDA or more the row is flagged and doubt includes 'ebitda'
method.revisions: every change a run made to a sourced figure or the acquirer (offer, consideration, deal value, premiums and the unaffected price, shares, LTM revenue, EBITDA and EBIT, net debt): run, field, from, to and cause (a reader version moving forward, a target re-identified, a reclassification, or read again), newest 20 kept. A re-read that fails, or that loses a figure without one of those causes, keeps the prior reading (readErrors says so); a run that would withdraw a figure from more than 5% of the rows carrying it is refused (scripts/precedent_transactions/guard.py)
method.flags: rows whose figures fail a sanity check (stock in the consideration, equity value far from the fee-table value, a premium above 150%, multiples out of range) are kept but flagged, and select() leaves them out
